page_title: Paul - The Simple PostgreSQL Client for Mac

sources.entry: Paul - AI-first PostgreSQL client for getting fast answers from your database with read-only access by default.

summary.name: Paul
summary.one_liner: Paul is a lightweight, AI-first PostgreSQL client for Mac that lets people query and browse a database in plain language, read-only by default.
use_cases: Investigating user issues in a production or staging database
Looking up customer data without waiting for an engineer
Giving a support team safe read access to PostgreSQL
Tracing relationships across tables without writing SQL
Quickly editing individual rows with a safety toggle
summary.what_it_does: Paul connects to any PostgreSQL database, including local, staging, or production instances. Users can ask questions in plain language and it turns them into queries without requiring SQL. It opens in read-only mode by default, and users can switch to an edit mode to run INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statements behind a clear safety toggle. The app supports browsing tables, following foreign keys, split-view across tables, and filtering and sorting data. The page says it is under 20MB and opens quickly, in contrast to heavier tools like pgAdmin and DBeaver.
notable: Read-only by default, with an explicit switch to edit mode
Natural-language questions turned into queries without SQL
Under 20MB with fast startup, positioned against pgAdmin, DBeaver and DataGrip
Foreign-key following and split-view across tables
caveats: Mac-only; no Windows or Linux version is mentioned on the page
Page says 'Free, no account required' but gives no details on limits or future paid tiers
Marketing-heavy page; performance claims such as 'opens in 2 seconds' are not independently verified
